title: Partitioning and clustering: the two decisions that define the bill

videos.script: Two decisions are made when a BigQuery table is created, and every query pays for them. {{two}} The first is how the table is cut into partitions. By day, by hour, by arrival, or by a range of numbers. {{partition}} A query that filters on that column reads only its own partitions. Any other filter reads them all. {{prune}} DuckDB prints which files it skips, so you will watch the pruning happen, and watch it fail. {{explain}} Cut too finely, and the same question opens sixteen times as many files. {{small}} The second decision is how the rows inside each partition are sorted. That is clustering. {{cluster}} Sorted by store, a filter on one store skips most of the day. {{skip}} Then both, priced together. At a thousand times Quitanda's size, the same dashboard costs two hundred and twenty dollars a month, or sixty-five cents. {{bill}}
